title: 3D Scatter Plot + LUT Color Mapping and Brush Selection
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement an interactive 3D scatter plot viewer that supports Lut color mapping, brush selection, range filtering, and real-time statistics.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
import { Lut } from 'three/addons/math/Lut.js';
</script>

[Dataset (500 Points, Generated with Hard-Coded Logic)]
Use a deterministic pseudorandom generator (a linear congruential generator with seed=42: state = (state * 1664525 + 1013904223) & 0xFFFFFFFF, normalized to [0,1]) to generate 500 data points. Each point contains:
- x: range [-10, 10]
- y: range [-10, 10]
- z: range [-10, 10]
- value: calculate from the coordinates using value = sin(x*0.5)*cos(z*0.3) + 0.5*(y/10), then normalize to [0, 1]
- label: divide into 5 levels according to value: "A"(0-0.2), "B"(0.2-0.4), "C"(0.4-0.6), "D"(0.6-0.8), "E"(0.8-1.0)

[Visualization (THREE.Points)]
(1) Use THREE.Points (BufferGeometry + PointsMaterial) to render all data points.
(2) The point size (size attribute) is determined by value: size = 0.1 + value * 0.4 (that is, within the range 0.1 to 0.5).
(3) Colors are mapped from value using Lut (from three/addons/math/Lut.js).
(4) A dropdown with id="colormap" switches the color mapping scheme. Its option values are: "rainbow", "cooltowarm", and "blackbody". Immediately update the colors of all points after switching.
(5) Set the Lut colormap range to the value range [min, max] of the currently visible points.

[Coordinate Axes and Ticks]
(6) Three orthogonal coordinate axis lines (one each for X/Y/Z), extending from -10 to 10.
(7) Place tick marks (small line segments + numeric labels) on each axis at -10, -5, 0, 5, and 10.
(8) Implement labels using CSS2DRenderer (from three/addons/renderers/CSS2DRenderer.js) or SpriteMaterial text textures. Axis labels: label the X axis "X", the Y axis "Y", and the Z axis "Z".

[Brush Selection]
(9) Implement rectangular brush selection: hold the left mouse button and drag to draw a rectangular region on the screen (a translucent rectangular overlay must be drawn). On release, mark all 3D points whose projections fall within that rectangle as "selected".
(10) Change the appearance of selected points (increase their size or change their color to white or a highlight color), and display the number selected in id="selectedCount".
(11) Clicking an empty area again clears the selection.

[Range Filter]
(12) Two range inputs: id="valueMin" (min=0, max=1, step=0.01, default 0) and id="valueMax" (min=0, max=1, step=0.01, default 1).
(13) After adjustment, make points whose value is outside the [valueMin, valueMax] range invisible (set the corresponding size to 0 or remove them from the geometry).
(14) Update the number of visible points in real time after filtering.

[Stats Panel]
(15) A DOM panel with id="stats" that displays real-time statistics for the currently visible points:
  - mean: arithmetic mean of the visible points' value values, to 4 decimal places
  - std: standard deviation of the visible points' value values (population standard deviation σ = sqrt(Σ(x-μ)²/N)), to 4 decimal places
  - min: minimum value among the visible points, to 4 decimal places
  - max: maximum value among the visible points, to 4 decimal places
  If there are no visible points, display 0 for all values.

[Camera and Controls]
(16) Use OrbitControls, with the initial camera position at (20, 15, 20), looking at the origin.

[State Exposure (Required, Updated Every Frame)]
window.__3D_STATE__ = {
  totalPoints: 500,
  visiblePoints: number,     // Number of currently visible (not filtered out) points
  selectedCount: number,     // Number of points selected by brush selection
  colormap: string,          // Current color mapping name
  valueRange: { min: number, max: number },  // Current filter range
  stats: {
    mean: number,  // Mean value of visible points (4-decimal-place precision)
    std: number,   // Standard deviation of the value values of visible points (4-decimal-place precision)
    min: number,   // Minimum value among visible points
    max: number    // Maximum value among visible points
  }
}

Output a single standalone HTML file that can run by being opened directly in a browser.
physics_constraints: 500 points generated with deterministic seed=42 LCG PRNG
Lut colormap from three/addons/math/Lut.js with rainbow/cooltowarm/blackbody
stats must match actual visible data: mean, std(population), min, max
brush selection uses screen-space rectangle projection
range filter hides points outside [valueMin, valueMax]
